tool.name: search_events
tool.title: Search Tech Week events
tool.description:
Search the official Tech Week calendar. This is the tool to reach for on any question about what is on, where, or when.

Call `list_filters` first when the person named a category, a neighborhood or a time of day: those arguments take keys from that catalogue, and a guessed key silently returns nothing — which reads exactly like a quiet week and will have you report the wrong answer confidently.

Every result carries the host's own one-line description and a link to the event's page on tech-week.com. Hand those links over directly — the page has the full description and the RSVP button, and the link never expires. There is no second call to make.

query.description: Free text matched against event name, host and company. Keep it to the distinctive words — "climate", "a16z" — and put anything that is a date, a city or a category in its own argument instead, where it filters exactly.

items.description: City slug from `list_cities`, e.g. "sf". Omit to search every city.

date.description: A single day, YYYY-MM-DD. One day only: there is no range. For "this weekend", call twice.

theme.description: Theme keys from `list_filters`. Keys, not labels — an invented value matches nothing and is indistinguishable from a quiet week.

format.description: Format keys from `list_filters` (dinner, happy hour, panel…).

track.description: Curated track keys from `list_filters` — editor-picked collections.

registration.description: Filter by the same values an event's `registration` reports. Pass ["open"] when the person intends to actually attend — it excludes events that are full or waitlisted. Pass ["open", "waitlist"] to include the ones with a queue. `invite_only` cannot be filtered on.

featuredOnly.description: Only editorially featured events. A good first call when someone has no specific ask.

sort.description: Default "time", which is almost always what you want.

limit.description: Results per page, 1–75, default 20. Out-of-range values are clamped, not rejected.

page.description: 1-based. `hasMore` tells you when to ask for the next one.
